RagShortTexts: Kozelsk resisted Mongol forces in 1238 before suffering severe destruction.
Prolonged defence needed food, repair labour and support, remembered differently by households.

Variants.Content: In 1238 Kozelsk resisted Mongol forces and suffered severe destruction after prolonged defence. Neighbours associate the town with refusal to yield easily, while households remember spent food, missing relatives and escape routes. Each further day required another allocation of provisions, repairs and care. Someone praising resistance from afar might know little of how individual families were scattered.

A position intended to gain time also needs aid, provisions and arrangements for withdrawal. Promised relief requires actual messages about its progress. A celebrated name cannot repay every family’s losses.

Defenders remember rotations, exhaustion and repairs. An enemy remaining outside does not prove food will last. Choosing a messenger and a receiving point helps resistance provide a real opportunity elsewhere.

Neighbours seek news of relatives inside the town or serving in a retinue. Wounded returnees need food and missing men’s fields need labour. Remembered courage and the needs of survivors belong to the same disaster.
